payload.report: Known brain and bone metastases with multiple prior treatment lines; the 42-year-old woman has cough, dyspnea, and chest pain. CT shows a lung lesion with alveolar septal changes and pleural effusion; follow-up CT shows enlargement with more nodules and effusion. Plasma cfDNA and pleural fluid NGS support metastatic involvement. The pathologist, radiologist, and laboratory physician unanimously favor metastatic pulmonary disease, while pulmonary thromboembolism, infection, and drug-induced lung injury lack supporting evidence (no CTPA/D-dimer, infection markers, or drug exposure). Convergent evidence establishes metastatic pulmonary disease.
